ns2:section.sectionText: Advanced GIS Methods and Applications in Social Science and Health Research: Recent developments in geographic information science (GIScience) have considerable potential to provide new insights to many analytical problems geographers, social scientists, and health researchers face in their research. This course introduces students to innovative advances in GIScience and geographic methods that can be applied in a wide range of research areas in geography, environmental health, urban studies and planning, transportation studies, and other fields. Topics include the spatial and temporal complexities of environmental influences, representing and measuring individual exposures to environmental influences, the uncertain geographic context problem (UGCoP), the neighborhood effect averaging problem (NEAP), selective mobility bias, and addressing contextual uncertainties through using dynamic analytical frameworks and high-resolution space-time data (e.g., GPS tracking data).
